newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones sees 2nd half profit down.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones sees 2nd half profit down.

text.p: Retailer David Jones Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its pre-tax profit in the second half of the 1996/97 financial year would be below that in the previous corresponding period.
David Jones said recent interest rate cuts should have a positive effect on consumer confidence and spending, but it did not expect any material improvement in retail conditions in the second half.
"Over the balance of the year, the company will continue to focus on implementing initiatives in product, consumer service and systems," the company said in a statement.
"However, at this stage it is anticipated that the profit before tax level in the second half will be below the same period last year."
David Jones earlier reported a 50 percent fall in first half net profit for the 26 weeks to January 25, 1997 to A$22.3 million from A$44.6 million.
Total earnings before interest and tax fell 33 percent to A$45.7 million from A$68.5 million.
David Jones said the results were slightly better than it had indicated in early January, due to improved clearance trading.
Sales were down one percent at A$782.6 million.
David Jones stores comparable store sales fell 2.9 percent, but rose 1.3 percent overall due to the impact of new stores.
